expectations.text: References the EDPB's draft Guidelines 03/2026 on web scraping in the context of generative AI, adopted July 2026 (consultation until October 30, 2026)
expectations.evidence: No reference to draft Guidelines 03/2026 (July 2026); only "ongoing EDPB and CNIL guidance" and Opinion 28/2024

expectations.text: States that consent is generally not viable as a lawful basis at scraping scale, making legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) the realistic basis
expectations.evidence: "Consent is rarely feasible at web-scraping scale"; legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f)) "the most commonly invoked basis for AI training"

expectations.text: Explains that legitimate interest requires a strict three-part balancing test with concrete mitigations/safeguards (e.g., excluding sensitive sources, respecting robots/opt-out signals, data minimisation)
expectations.evidence: "structured three-step test: (a) identify a legitimate interest, (b)... necessary, (c) balance"; mitigations incl. excluding sensitive sites, robots.txt, opt-out signals, minimisation

expectations.text: States that controllers are expected to publish detailed public privacy notices about the scraping (Art. 14 transparency)
expectations.evidence: Art. 14 discussed: "publish clear, accessible information about training data sources and purposes"

expectations.text: Mentions facilitating data subject rights including pre-collection opt-out mechanisms, and that the guidance covers first-party scraping, contracted scraping, and purchased broker datasets
expectations.evidence: Mentions rights mechanisms and opt-out signals ('noai' tags, Do Not Train registries) but never covers the guidance applying to contracted scraping and purchased broker datasets
